definitions.explanation: The act of reading books, magazines, or manga at a bookstore or convenience store without purchasing them.

examples.japanese: {立|た}ち{読|よ}み⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: To read (a book/magazine) while standing in the store.

examples.japanese: ⟦コンビニ→コンビニ：01081_konbini⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{漫画|まんが}→漫画：01511_manga⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{立|た}ち{読|よ}み⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧がいた。
examples.english: There was someone reading manga at the convenience store without buying it.

examples.japanese: {立|た}ち{読|よ}み⟦{禁止|きんし}→禁止：02643_kinshi⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{書|か}いてある→書く：00477_kaku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧、⟦{気|き}にしない→気にする：03026_kinisuru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: Even though it says 'no standing reading,' some people don't care.

notes:
USAGE:
Can be used as a ⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ verb: {立|た}ち{読|よ}み⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧. This practice is common in Japanese convenience stores and bookstores. Some stores now wrap magazines in plastic or post {立|た}ち{読|よ}み⟦{禁止|きんし}→禁止：02643_kinshi⟧ (no standing reading) signs to discourage it.

CULTURAL NOTE:
While often tolerated, {立|た}ち{読|よ}み is generally considered somewhat inconsiderate. However, it remains a familiar scene in Japanese daily life, especially at convenience stores.

ETYMOLOGY:
⟦{立|た}つ→立つ：00758_tatsu⟧ (to stand) + ⟦{読|よ}む→読む：00426_yomu⟧ (to read). A straightforward compound describing the action.
